newsitem.title: UK: EIU sees cocoa supply deficit at 20,000 T in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: EIU sees cocoa supply deficit at 20,000 T in 96/97.

text.p: The Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) projected a world cocoa deficit of 20,000 tonnes in the current 1996/97 season (October-September) after an estimated surplus of 150,000 in 1995/96.
In its latest quarterly report on commodities, the EIU forecast total grindings at 2.665 million tonnes from 2.647 million a year ago and production at 2.645 million tonnes from 2.800 million.
"For 1996/97 we now see supply doing better than previously projected because recent rains appear to have done more good than harm in Cote d'Ivoire by improving pod survival chances," it said.
It pegged the Ivorian harvest at one million tonnes for 1996/97, up from 1.2 million last season.
Current stocks were higher than expected and declines in the coming season would be slower than previously projected, it said.

The stocks/consumption ratio, a key barometer of prices, was forecast at 52 percent for 1996/97 from 53 percent in 1995/96. Prices have rallied each time the ratio fell below the 30 percent mark in the past.
Ghana, the world's second largest producer, was seen harvesting 360,000 tonnes compared with 375,000 a year ago.
The EIU expected prices to retrench in the short-term, then gradually rise until the end of the 1997/98 season due to projected declines in stocks.
It forecast the 1997/98 production at 2.635 million tonnes and grindings at 2.730 million.

"1997/98 projections assume that the weather will be less kind than in recent years to the development of the Ivorian crop which appears to be establishing itself at a much higher level than seemed possible just a year or so ago," the EIU said.
The Ivorian output was seen at 970,000 tonnes and Ghana at 370,000. The world supply deficit was put at 95,000 tonnes.
Global stocks at the end of 1997/98 were forecast at 47.3 percent of consumption, compared with 39.2 previously projected. -- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8072
